title: Improving Generalization in Federated Learning by Seeking Flat Minima
main_claims: Federated learning models converge to sharp minima due to statistical heterogeneity of client data, which explains their poor generalization.
Applying SAM or ASAM on the client-side during local training substantially reduces Hessian eigenvalues and improves generalization in both homogeneous and heterogeneous federated settings.
Combining client-side SAM/ASAM with server-side SWA achieves the best generalization performance, with FedASAM+SWA reducing λ_max from 93.46 to 24.57 in the heterogeneous scenario.
methodology: Hessian eigenspectrum analysis (power iteration to compute top-50 eigenvalues) is used to characterize sharpness of federated models. SAM, ASAM, and SWA are integrated into FedAvg: SAM/ASAM replace SGD in the local client training loop; SWA averages server-side models cyclically from 75% of training. Experiments span CIFAR-10/100, Landmarks-User-160k, and IDDA semantic segmentation across heterogeneous (Dirichlet α∈{0,0.5}) and homogeneous (α=1000) settings.
key_results: FedASAM reduces λ_max from 93.46 (FedAvg) to 30.11 in the heterogeneous setting (α=0) on CIFAR-100.
FedASAM+SWA further reduces λ_max to 24.57 and achieves 42.01% accuracy (vs. 30.25% for FedAvg E=1) in the most heterogeneous setting.
The combination of SAM/ASAM and SWA consistently outperforms each method individually across all federated scenarios and tasks.
limitations: Federated setting introduces communication overhead and heterogeneity that differ fundamentally from the centralized setting studied in the RQ; direct transferability of findings is limited.
Hessian eigenvalue analysis measures sharpness but is not paired with representation stability (CKA) measurements, limiting interpretation of the relative contributions of flatness vs. other factors.
SAM doubles local training computation per round, which is more costly in the federated setting than in centralized training.
relevance_to_rq: Relevant to the flat_minima_for_dg and weight_averaging sub-topics: provides empirical evidence that flat minima (low λ_max) correlate with better generalization under distribution heterogeneity, and that SAM and SWA are complementary flat-minima methods. The Hessian eigenvalue analysis methodology is directly analogous to the sharpness measurement planned in the RQ's experiment.

key_quotes.text: we show that both converge to sharp minima, providing a plausible explanation for the highlighted lack of generalization
key_quotes.context: Loss landscape analysis finding that FedAvg converges to sharp minima in both heterogeneous and homogeneous scenarios
Quantitative Hessian eigenvalue result showing combined SAM+SWA achieves the lowest sharpness

key_quotes.text: By seeking parameters in neighborhoods having uniform low loss, the model converges towards flatter minima and its generalization significantly improves in both homogeneous and heterogeneous scenarios
key_quotes.context: Summary of the paper's main finding on flat minima and federated generalization

extraction_issues: evidence_strength is mixed: Hessian analysis is correlational (sharpness vs. generalization), while SAM/ASAM vs. FedAvg ablations are controlled but confounded by FL-specific factors.
